questions.question: Which underserved segment of the supply chain finance market is a key focus of the partnership signed between the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Standard Chartered Bank in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distributor financing for downstream players**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**
__
• The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** and **Standard Chartered Bank** have partnered to boost **supply chain finance** in India through risk-sharing arrangements for both **USD** and **Rupee** transactions.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**
__
• The partnership specifically targets **distributor financing**, which is described as an underserved segment of the market in India.
• By focusing on **distributor finance transactions**, the initiative aims to unlock **working capital** for **downstream players**, which are often **Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)**.
• The collaboration marks **ADB's first engagement** in the **distributor finance space** within the Indian market.
• The arrangement involves two facilities: a **GIFT City-based facility** for **US dollar-denominated transactions** and a **partial guarantee facility** for **onshore rupee transactions**.
• Other options like infrastructure debt or agricultural commodity financing are not the primary focus of this specific **ADB-Standard Chartered** agreement.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
__
• The agreements were signed by **ADB Vice-President Bhargav Dasgupta** and **Standard Chartered Bank's India & South Asia CEO P D Singh**.
• The partnership extends **ADB's risk-sharing capacity** into both **offshore and onshore segments** of the Indian market.
• The primary goal is to enhance **supply chain resilience** and support the flow of **cross-border and domestic trade**.
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• The initiative aligns with **ADB's strategic priority** to promote **inclusive economic growth** and **financial deepening** across the **Asia and Pacific** region.
• Access to finance is considered a binding constraint for businesses managing **working capital** and participating in **global trade**.</ul

questions.question: What was India's real GDP growth rate for the full financial year 2025-26, according to the latest data released in June 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.7%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**
__
• India’s **GDP growth** data for the fourth quarter (Q4) and the full financial year **2025-26** was released, showing a robust performance that beat previous estimates.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**
__
• For the **whole financial year 2025-26**, India's real GDP growth stood at **7.7%**. This figure is marginally higher than the previous government estimates of **7.6%**.
• In the **fourth quarter (Q4)** of FY26 (January-March), the economy grew at **7.8%**, which was better than market expectations.
• Sectoral performance during the fourth quarter showed that **Trade, hotels, transport, and communication** expanded the most at **12.5%**, followed by **Financial and real estate services** at **10.4%**.
• Manufacturing registered a growth of **7.3%**, while the **construction sector** grew by **8.4%** during the quarter.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
__
• At constant prices, the **real GDP** for the full year 2025-26 is projected to reach **Rs 323.12 lakh crore**, compared to Rs 299.89 lakh crore in FY 2024-25.
• The **Nominal GDP** for FY 2025-26 is estimated at **Rs 346.36 lakh crore**, representing an annual increase of **8.9%**.
• For the **Q4 (Jan-Mar)** specifically, nominal GDP growth was **9.1%**, reaching **Rs 94.65 lakh crore**.
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

• Despite global uncertainties like the **US-Iran conflict**, India remains the world's **fastest-growing major economy**.
• Economists at **ICRA** have warned that growth might slow to **sub-6.5% in FY2027** due to factors like elevated energy prices and potential **El Nino** conditions affecting agriculture.
• **Sujan Hajra**, Chief Economist at Anand Rathi Financial Services, noted that an expansion of around **7%** in FY27 appears reachable if consumption and investment remain favorable.

questions.question: Which bank became the first in the Asia-Pacific region to pilot 'Visa Intelligent Commerce' for everyday payments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DBS Bank.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **On February 16, 2026, DBS Bank and Visa announced a joint pilot under 'Visa Intelligent Commerce' (VIC) to drive the future of "agent-initiated" payments.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Landmark:** DBS is the **first issuer in Asia Pacific** to pilot this technology, which allows AI agents to complete everyday tasks (like food and beverage orders) on behalf of customers using DBS/POSB credit and debit cards.
 
• **Agentic Commerce:** The pilot focuses on "agentic commerce," where trusted AI agents use **AI-ready credentials** (tokenized card details) to execute transactions within secure, issuer-controlled boundaries.
 
• **Trusted Agent Protocol:** The collaboration utilizes Visa's secure infrastructure and the **Trusted Agent Protocol** to ensure that all automated payments are consent-driven, transparent, and protected by rigorous authentication checks.
 
• **Real-world Application:** The initial phase successfully demonstrated real-world food and beverage transactions. Future trials are set to expand into online retail and travel bookings.
 
• **AI Trends:** The move aligns with high AI adoption in Singapore, where a study found that **77% of residents** use generative AI tools in daily life and 80% rely on AI assistance for online shopping.
 
• **Leadership:** **Ananya Sen** (Group Head of Regional Consumer Products, DBS Bank) and **T.R. Ramachandran** (Head of Products & Solutions, Asia Pacific, Visa) noted that this sets new standards for the next generation of cards and payments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Glossary__**

__
 
• Agentic Commerce__: A system where autonomous AI agents act as intermediaries to research and execute purchases for users.
 
• __Tokenisation__: The process of replacing sensitive card data with a unique digital identifier (token) to enhance payment security.

questions.question: Which bank has introduced a Demat Viewing Facility through its WhatsApp Banking platform to enhance digital investor services?

questions.question: What is the total value of the 'Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool' (BMIP) launched by the Ministry of Finance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**USD 1.5 billion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Department of Financial Services (DFS)** under the **Ministry of Finance** has launched the **'Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool' (BMIP)**.
 
• The pool aims to provide continuous maritime insurance coverage amid current **Middle East tensions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pool Size:** The total value of the newly launched **Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)** is **USD 1.5 billion**. Therefore, option 4 is correct.
 
• **Sovereign Guarantee:** The pool is backed by a sovereign guarantee of **USD 1.4 billion (₹12,980 crores)** from the government to act as a safety net.
 
• **Administration:** **GIC Re** serves as the pool administrator and will submit returns, details of reinsurance arrangements, and performance statements.
 
• **First Policy Issued:** The first **Marine Hull & Machinery War Policy** document under BMIP was handed over to **M/s. Hoger Offshore and Marine Private Limited**, issued by **The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Coverage Details:** The pool covers all maritime risks, including **Hull and Machinery, Cargo, P&I (Protection and Indemnity), and War risks**.
 
• **Target Audience:** The insurance is designated for Indian-flagged or controlled vessels, or vessels destined to or originating from **India**.
 
• **Claim Servicing:** For claims up to **USD 100 million**, the pool will use its own capacity. The sovereign guarantee will only be invoked for claims exceeding this amount, acting as a contingent backstop of last resort.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The initiative will strengthen **India’s sovereign control over maritime trade** and ensure trade continuity despite potential withdrawals of international insurance due to geopolitical tensions or sanctions.
 
• This mechanism ultimately strengthens India's maritime risk protection framework and promotes the nation's financial sovereignty on the global stage.

questions.question: Which bank recently partnered with Flipkart and PayU to launch biometric card payments on the e-commerce platform?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Flipkart**, **Axis Bank**, and **PayU** announced the launch of **biometric authentication** for card payments on the e-commerce platform.
 
• This feature allows **Axis Bank cardholders** to approve transactions using their **fingerprint** or **Face ID**, ditching the traditional **one-time password (OTP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__

• The initiative positions **Flipkart** among the first major Indian e-commerce platforms to offer this capability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Regulatory Backing:** The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** issued its **‘Authentication Mechanisms for Digital Payment Transactions Directions, 2025’** circular, which explicitly encourages biometric and risk-based authentication over **SMS OTPs**.
 
• **Security Upgrades:** The three companies emphasize that the system reduces exposure to **SIM-swap** and **OTP-interception fraud** through device binding and enhanced security checks.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Gaurav Arora**, Vice President of Payments at **Flipkart**, stated that the integration meets regulatory requirements while reducing friction for shoppers.
 
• **Arnika Dixit**, President and Head of Cards at **Axis Bank**, highlighted the bank's intent to extend such innovations alongside the growth of digital commerce.
 
• **Hemang Dattani**, Chief Business Officer at **PayU Payments**, described the launch as a crucial step towards a faster and more secure checkout experience.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Reserve Bank of India introduced relaxed norms for project finance provisioning bringing significant relief to lenders, with effect from _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 October 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced **relaxed prudential norms for project finance provisioning** to ease the regulatory burden on banks and financial institutions.
 
• The revised norms were scheduled to come into force from **1 October 2025**.
 
• The relaxation aimed to support lenders involved in financing large **infrastructure projects** such as **roads, power, ports, and telecom**.
 
• Under the new framework, provisioning requirements during the **construction phase** of infrastructure projects were reduced compared to earlier proposals.
 
• The move was expected to improve **credit flow to infrastructure projects**, reduce stress on lenders, and encourage long-term project financing.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 2.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• Established in **1935** under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• Headquarters: **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
• Current functions include **monetary policy regulation**, **bank supervision**, and **financial stability management**.
 
 
 
• **Project Finance**
 
 
• Refers to long-term financing of infrastructure and industrial projects where repayment is primarily dependent on **project cash flows**.
 
• Common sectors include **power generation**, **transport infrastructure**, **urban infrastructure**, and **renewable energy**.
 
 
 
• **Provisioning in Banking**
 
 
• Provisioning refers to the funds banks must set aside to cover **potential loan losses**.
 
• It is a key regulatory measure used by the RBI to maintain **banking system stability**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Reform**
 
 
• Supports the expansion of **infrastructure investment** in India.
 
• Reduces capital pressure on banks financing large projects.
 
• Improves the overall **credit growth in infrastructure sector**.

questions.question: What is the total outlay of the Ministry of Defence in the Union Budget 2026-27 and what is the percentage increase compared to the Budget Estimates of FY 2025-26?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹7.85 lakh crore; 15 per cent.**__

• Around ₹1.39 lakh crore, nearly 75 per cent of the capital acquisition budget, has been earmarked for procurement from domestic industries.

 __

 __

questions.question: The depreciation of the Indian rupee in recent times is primarily associated with which of the following factors?

options.text: Increase in agricultural exports and surplus current account balance
Decline in global crude oil prices and rising remittances
Rising crude oil prices and foreign institutional investor (FII) outflows
Increase in foreign exchange reserves and capital inflows

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Indian rupee depreciated to ₹93.71 per dollar amid rising crude oil prices and significant outflows of foreign institutional investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Rising crude oil prices increase India’s import bill, widening the current account deficit and exerting downward pressure on the rupee. **Hence, Option 3 is correct. **
 
• Increase in agricultural exports and a surplus current account balance would strengthen the rupee due to higher foreign exchange inflows. **Hence, Option 1 is incorrect. **
 
• Decline in global crude oil prices reduces import costs and improves the current account balance, which supports the rupee rather than weakening it. **Hence, Option 2 is incorrect. **
 
• Increase in foreign exchange reserves and capital inflows leads to higher supply of foreign currency and strengthens the rupee. **Hence, Option 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Current Account Deficit (CAD): Difference between imports and exports of goods and services.
 
• FII Outflows: Lead to selling of domestic assets and increase demand for foreign currency.
 
• Oil Price Sensitivity: India imports a large share of its crude oil needs, making the rupee vulnerable to global price fluctuations.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of 'Project Sa-Mudra' as outlined in the Reserve Bank of India’s ‘Utkarsh 2029’ strategy?

options.text: Expanding central bank digital currency for cross-border payments
Scaling up the Unified Lending Interface to widen credit access
Developing regulatory frameworks for quantum computing

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Modernizing currency management**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has unveiled its medium-term strategy framework, **‘Utkarsh 2029’**, to be implemented from **April 2026 to March 2029**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project Sa-Mudra:** As per the **Utkarsh 2029** framework, this specific project is a long-term initiative dedicated to **modernizing currency management**.
 
• **Expansion of CBDC:** While the strategy mentions expanding **Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)**, its primary goal is to ensure **efficient cross-border payments**, not currency management modernization.
 
• **Unified Lending Interface (ULI):** The **ULI** is intended to be scaled up specifically to **widen credit access** and improve financial inclusion.
 
• **Emerging Technologies:** The RBI plans to develop **regulatory frameworks** for advanced technologies like **artificial intelligence (AI)** and **quantum computing** to address evolving technological challenges.
 
• The core logic is that **Project Sa-Mudra** is the designated name for the modernization of the physical and traditional currency infrastructure within the 2026-2029 roadmap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The strategy is structured around **six pillars**: robust regulation, customer-centric and inclusive finance, competitive markets, effective technology, a future-ready organisation, and a global India focus.
 
• The framework also emphasizes the **internationalisation of the rupee** and the **global expansion of UPI**.
 
• Technical upgrades include **e-Kuber 3.0** and the development of an indigenous **AI-based supervisory system**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Utkarsh 2029** follows the previous **Utkarsh 2.0** roadmap.
 
• RBI Governor **Sanjay Malhotra** stated that the plan addresses **technological, geopolitical, and climate-related challenges**.
 
• The framework includes **simplifying regulations** by rationalising master directions to reduce compliance burdens.

questions.question:
​With reference to the 16th Finance Commission (FC16**)** and its recommendations for the award period 2026–2031, which of the following statements is correct?

​

options.text: The 16th Finance Commission has introduced "Tax and Fiscal Effort" as a new criterion for horizontal devolution to reward states with better fiscal discipline. ​
The Commission has recommended a significant increase in the vertical devolution of the divisible pool, raising the states' share from 41% to 45%. ​
For horizontal devolution, the 16th Finance Commission has introduced "Contribution to GDP" as a new criterion with a 10% weightage to reward economically productive states. ​
The Commission has decided to use the 1971 Census data as the primary basis for population-related weightage to protect the interests of states that successfully controlled population growth. ​

questions.solution:
​The correct answer is **Option 3**.

​**Key Points: **

 
• ​**The core topic** is the evolving formula for horizontal devolution (distribution among states) introduced by the 16th Finance Commission compared to the previous commission.
 
• ​**Option A:** This is incorrect. The "Tax and Fiscal Effort" criterion, which had a 2.5% weightage in FC15, was actually **dropped** by the 16th Finance Commission.
 
• ​**Option B:** This is incorrect. The Union Government has accepted the recommendation to maintain the vertical devolution at **41%**, the same level as the 15th Finance Commission.
 
• ​**Option C:****This is correct.** A major change in the FC16 formula is the introduction of **"Contribution to GDP"** as a new criterion with a **10% weightage**, which aims to incentivize states contributing more to the national economy.
 
• ​**Option D:** This is incorrect. The Commission has continued the shift toward using the **2011 Census** data (with an increased weightage of 17.5% compared to FC15's 15%), though "Demographic Performance" is used as a separate criterion to balance the interests of states with lower fertility rates.

​**Additional Information: **

 
• ​**Horizontal Devolution Formula (FC16): **

 
 
• ​**Income Distance:** 42.5% (Reduced from 45% in FC15)
 
• ​**Population (2011 Census):** 17.5% (Increased from 15% in FC15)
 
• ​**Area:** 10% (Reduced from 15% in FC15)
 
• ​**Demographic Performance:** 10% (Reduced from 12.5% in FC15)
 
• ​**Forest Cover:** 10% (Maintained at the same level)
 
• ​**Contribution to GDP:** 10% (New Criterion)
 
 
 
• ​**Vertical Devolution Stability:** By keeping the share at 41%, the Union maintains budgetary predictability while handling structural fiscal reforms and off-budget liabilities.
 
• ​**Divisible Pool:** This refers to the portion of Gross Tax Revenue (GTR) that is shared with states. While GTR grows, the "Divisible Pool" as a percentage of GTR has seen fluctuations over the last decade due to the use of cesses and surcharges.
 
• ​**Mandate:** Apart from tax sharing, FC16 is tasked with reviewing disaster management financing and suggesting a roadmap for fiscal consolidation to reduce the deficit.

questions.question: India’s objection to selective tariff targeting by a trading partner is primarily rooted in which WTO principle?

options.text: The principle that prohibits any country from offering tariff concessions during balance-of-payments crises
The principle that mandates uniform tariff bindings for all members regardless of bilateral relations
The principle that forbids discriminatory treatment among members except under permitted arrangements
The principle that allows developing nations to impose retaliatory duties without dispute settlement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• EAM S. Jaishankar raised concerns about the U.S. selectively imposing higher tariffs on India’s oil-linked trade, arguing this violates established global trade norms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• WTO’s Most Favoured Nation (MFN) principle requires non-discriminatory treatment among all members unless within exceptions such as FTAs, special preference schemes, or security exemptions. **Hence, Option 3 is correct. **
 
• WTO does not prohibit tariff concessions during balance-of-payments crises; instead, BOP provisions allow temporary restrictions by the affected country itself. **Hence, Option 1 is incorrect. **
 
• Tariff bindings are member-specific, negotiated individually, and not uniform across members. **Hence, Option 2 is incorrect. **
 
• Developing countries can impose retaliatory duties only after a formal WTO dispute ruling; unilateral retaliation is not permitted. **Hence, Option 4 is incorrect.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MFN Principle (GATT Article I)**: No discriminatory tariffs between trading partners.
 
• **National Treatment (GATT Article III)**: Imported products must be treated no less favorably than domestic products.
 
• **Tariff Bindings**: Commitments negotiated bilaterally with schedules differing by country.
 
• **Dispute Settlement Body (DSB)**: Authorizes retaliation only after ruling compliance failure.
 
• **India’s consistent position**: Opposes unilateral, selective tariff measures as violations of a rules-based multilateral order.
